title.narrative: LPI - Innovative and Holistic Peacebuilding in Eastern DRC
LPI - Innovativt och holistiskt fredsbyggande i östra DRK

description.narrative: The overall objective of this programme is to develop participatory and innovative approaches to address some of the root causes of conflict to contribute to peace and stability in Eastern DRC (North Kivu, South Kivu, and Maniema). The geographical focus is in North and South Kivu provinces. The most problematic territories (except Beni) in the two key provinces will be targeted although in practice some territories will see more activities than others (Rutshuru, Masisi, Walikale, for example for North Kivu, and Fizi, Uvira, Kalehe, Mwenga in South Kivu. LPI has partners in these territories. In Maniema, only run a situation analysis will be conducted. LPI’s three organisational strategic priorities are:– 1. Civil society support and inclusive engagement for peace; 2. Policy Engagement and Awareness-Raising; and 3. Knowledge and Learning to enhance practice – will function as an overarching framework for programming. Changes in four outcome areas are needed to promote the overall objective:Outcome 1: Community-level conflict actors work together to design and implement new holistic conflict transformation strategies that address the root causes of conflict.Outcome 2: Women and young people participate in and influence stabilisation and peacebuilding processes and become recognised as actors of social change.Outcome 3: Political, security, judicial and other leaders at local, provincial, national, regional and international levels, supported by LPI and partners, take actions to create an environment more conducive to peace in the DRC and the Great Lakes region.Outcome 4: Increased individual and collective capacity of civil society actors and community peace structures to promote more transformative peacebuilding.

Genom denna insats stödjer Sida genomförandet av Life and Peace Institute (LPI) landprogram i DRK (2021-2025). Landprogrammet fokuserar på att påskynda fredsbyggande ur ett perspektiv från flera aktörer (inklusive lokalt på befolkningsnivå, inom civilsamhället samt på provinsnivå) i östra DRK. Detta kommer att uppnås genom en innovativ strategi baserad på kombinationen av samhällsledda processer för konflikttransformation, stärkning av lokala civilsamhällesorganisationer, deltagande av kvinnor och ungdomar i fredsbyggande processer, inklusive förstärkning av samhällenas motståndskraft mot konflikter. Programmet kommer att arbeta med att skapa nya ansvarsförhållanden mellan staten, befolkningen och andra intressenter (på alla nivåer). Detta arbete på lokal nivå, inom det civila samhället och på provinsnivå kommer att bidra till och ingå i fredsprocesser på nationell och regional nivå.

Through this contribution, Sida supports the implementation of Life and Peace Institute’s (LPI) DRC country programme (2021-2025). The programme focuses on accelerating peacebuilding interventions from a multi-actors' perspective (including at community, civil society and policy levels) in eastern DRC. This will be achieved through an innovative and participatory approach based on the combination of community-led conflict transformation processes, strengthening local civil society organizations, participation of women and youth in peacebuilding processes, including strengthening communities' resilience to conflicts. The programme will work on creating new accountability loops between the state, populations and all stakeholders (at all levels) that collective responses to complex conflict issues are implemented in a participatory, collaborative, sustainable and conflict sensitive manner. This work at community and provincial level will feed into peace processes at national and regional levels.(2021-2025) which focuses on accelerating peacebuilding interventions from a multi-actors' perspective (including at community, civil society and policy levels) in Eastern DRC. sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The Namna Mpya ya Ujenzi wa Amani (NMUA) Programme, led by the Life & Peace Institute (LPI) and civil society partners in the DRC, operated under worsening security conditions in North and South Kivu and Ituri, which further eroded social cohesion.
Programme Implementation:
Partners: Started with 10 partners in 2021; reduced progressively to 6 (2022), 4 (2023), and 2 (2024).
In its inception year, LPI started with 10 implementing partners ( Action pour le Développement et la Paix Endogènes (ADEPAE), Action pour la Paix et la Concorde (APC), Réseau des Cadres de Concertation Intercommunautaire (RCCI), Save Communities in Conflicts (SCC), Solidarité des Volontaires pour lHumanité (SVH), Action pour le Développement des Milieux Ruraux (ADMR), Dynamique des Femmes Juristes (DFJ), Réseau des Associations Congolaises des Jeunes (RACOJ), Service par, pour et avec les femmes (SEPPAF), Union Paysanne pour Developpement Intégral (UPDI)) , fostering meaningful engagement with technical and political authorities, and rebuilding constructive relationships with diverse stakeholders in the peacebuilding sector to enhance collaboration and coordination. In the following years, the number of partners has been reduced as follows, including 6 partners (APC, RCCI, SVH, ADMR, UPDI, RACOJ) for the year 2022, 4 partners (RCCI, SVH, UPDI and ADMR) for the year 2023 and only 2 (ADMR and SVH) for the year 2024. LPI and its partners consolidated programme achievements to drive positive change within communities and among targeted stakeholders.
LPI reduced the number of partners due to a lack of funds, mainly because 43% of the LPI programme was funded by Sida and the remainder could not be secured; furthermore, security concerns forced the programme to withdraw from certain areas due to the war.
In community level, the reduction in the number of partners negatively affected some initial target areas, especially the chiefdoms of BashaliMokoto, Bwisha, in North-Kivu; Nindja, Kelehe and Walungu in South-Kivu which had to be abandoned early in the process. It also weakened sustainability at that level including resolutions that were not followed up in these zones. Additional disruption arose from the M23 occupation, during which both local and customary administrations because were replaced.
It should be noted, however, that cooperation with the authorities has been strengthened, community-based peace-building structures (involving women and young people) have been supported, and conflict resolution and stakeholder participation have been encouraged.
Key Achievements Across Four Levels
1. Community-Based Peacebuilding In the final evaluation report, the evaluators noted a significant reduction in hate speech that undermines peaceful coexistence between communities in the Fizi and Uvira districts, achieved through the inter-community consultation frameworks established to monitor the situation during this sensitive period of tension. This has resulted in certain leaders and members of the Bafuliru and Banyamulenge communities adopting a moderate stance in their contributions during workshops and/or in certain public speeches.
The inter-community consultation framework brings together committees of elders from each group within each territory. They have initiated dialogues with local communities to facilitate the free movement of people and goods between the two groups. The elders committee of the Lemera group launched a dialogue that helped to ease tensions between the Bafuliiru and Banyamulenge communities, which were in conflict over the management of the Rurambo area. These processes have enabled members of the Banyamulenge community to move freely along the Kitoga-Kahololo route and allowed more than 40 households to return to their villages.
2. Women and Youth Empowerment
In terms of inclusion (gender sensitivity and inclusive programming), LPI ensured that all categories of people (women, men, boys, girls, people with disabilities, indigenous peoples) were represented in a balanced manner and that their representation created possibilities to influence decisions and meaningful opportunities to address the specific needs and interests of all these categories.
For illustration purposes, gender and inclusion were considered in the following ways:
Women's structures were supported in their approach to implementing peace activities at the local level in the intervention areas Women and youth were supported in acquiring land titles to combat land insecurity and deprivation, which this category often suffers from in the intervention areas. The Participatory Action Research conducted in the Fizi territory specifically addressed the issue of inclusive local governance in relation to the integration of Pygmée peoples (PAP). This process resulted in the granting of land and customary land titles to more than 40 PAPs, primarily women and youth. This demonstrates our commitment to understanding and valuing the experiences of indigenous peoples and including them in governance processes.
3. Policy Engagement
Integrated peacebuilding principles into the National Programme for Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Recovery and Stabilization (P DDRCS) strategy. Secured land for returnees and supported development of Local Development Plans and Provincial Operations Plans. The LPI programme provided technical and financial support to the provincial office when drafting its Provincial Operational Plan and equipped the South Kivu office with furniture. As lead of the eastern DRC stabilization actions in line with the presidential decree mandating the PDDRCS to coordinate all stabilization efforts, LPI worked closely with PDDRCS and set up the Peacebuilding Community of Practice (CPP) platform, now become key tool for coordination of national and international peace actors and pushing dialogue initiatives connecting to peace processes.
Strengthened customary conflict resolution mechanisms.
4. Coordination of Peacebuilding Interventions
Enhanced capacities of 10 CSOs , Produced advocacy notes and organized missions in Kinshasa and internationally (Berlin, Stockholm, Brussels, New York, Washington DC). Participated in regional forums and organized workshops on gender and conflict analysis with partners like FBA. Improvement of technical and organizational capacities of 10 civil society organisations (CSOs), through accompaniment approaches to lead peacebuilding processes which address major conflict issues in eastern DRC.
Elaboration of more than 5 advocacy notes (see annexes) and organised advocacy missions in Kinshasa and the Great Lakes region. Participation on 29 January 2024, in the workshop organised by the Association Episcopal dAfrique Centrale (ACEAC) in Goma and development of a common Advocacy Note related to peace processes in Eastern DRC. Attending meetings in Berlin (5 June 2024), Stockholm (28 May to 31 May 2024), Brussels (3 June 2024), New York (11 to 15 November 2024) and Washington DC (18 to 21 November 2024) related to the conflict in East of DRC.
Presentation of CPPs analysis of the regional conflict dynamics at the regional forum in Bujumbura organised by the Swiss Embassy and the Office of the Special Representative of the UN in the Great Lake's Region from 4 to 5 March 2024. Support to the Women Forum of the Assemblée des Evêques de la Province Ecclésiastique de Bukavu (ASSEPB) area (Bukavu, Goma, Butembo, Uvira, Kasongo and Kindu) on capacity development in social cohesion and peacebuilding from 20 to 24 August 2024.
In collaboration with Folke Bernadotte Academy (FBA), organization of a conflict analysis workshop and positioning of peace actors regarding the actual crisis in Eastern DRC, in Nairobi from 17-18 March 2025. 19 March 2025, Organisation in Nairobi, in collaboration with FBA, of a workshop to follow up on the training on: A gender perspective in peace and security activities in the DRC: North and South Kivu, provided by FBA and RCPI for CPP members in December 2024 in Bukavu.
From 29 to 30 April 2025, in collaboration with FBA, LPI held a workshop to harmonise views, areas of complementarity, and possible avenues for collaboration between CENCO (Conférence Episcopale Nationale du Congo), Eglise du Christ au Congo (ECC) and CPP, to contribute to the content of the social pact for peace and harmonious coexistence through the thematic reference frameworks produced by the CENCO pact, and propose expertise within the CPP that could support various commissions in the production of these reference frameworks.
To sustain LPIs achievements, consultations were conducted with peace community structures, local authorities, community and religious leaders to identify the best approaches to ensure that the latter can take over at the conclusion of the program. Therefore, the closing of the program was marked by the strengthening of the achievements through increased accountability of local peace structures, women and youth, as well as community leaders in the negotiation and mediation of local conflicts, awareness-raising and advocacy.
